description: At the crossroads of matter, code, and space, astrecho imagines habitats that breathe with the cosmos. We merge material alchemy with algorithmic precision to shape environments that resonate across planetary frontiers. Our goal is to weave chemical cycles and structural grace into living ecosystems. Together, we translate raw data into poetic shelters, crafting the echoes of tomorrow into spaces that sustain life.
summary:
Since the 1960s, NASA has left an incredible trail of rovers, landers, and probes across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. But what happens
to these silent pioneers?
Enter C.U.R.I.O.—an immersive virtual museum and interactive storytelling experience guided by a friendly robotic caretaker! C.U.R.I.O.
breathes new life into forgotten space hardware, inviting young space enthusiasts to explore the actual machines that made history
possible. Through stunning 3D models, digital storybooks, engineering secrets, and interactive quizzes, space exploration history transforms
into an epic adventure.
C.U.R.I.O. is more than just a digital exhibit; it’s a bridge across generations. By turning technical engineering milestones into an exciting,
accessible journey, it preserves the legacy of human ingenuity and sparks wonder in the next wave of cosmic explorers!
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Our project is an immersive, interactive storytelling experience that takes users on a journey to discover the forgotten machines humans sent into space. Guided by C.U.R.I.O. (Caretaker of Unheard Robots In Orbit), a friendly, old-fashioned robotic caretaker, visitors explore three destinations: the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.

Users travel through NASA-inspired environments, walk across real planetary panoramas, discover abandoned space machines, and listen to their stories. Each discovery combines interactive NASA 3D models, real archival photographs, narrated films, and four storytelling chapters covering each machine's journey, from its creation to its final mission.

To make learning interactive, users answer two questions about each machine to earn a stamp in their digital Space Explorer Passport. Collecting all three stamps unlocks a printable Space Relic Historian certificate.

The experience also includes Ask C.U.R.I.O., an AI-powered assistant that answers questions using a database of verified NASA information, with references and citations.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Educational: Makes complex space exploration history easier and more engaging to understand.
  • Accessible: Presents scientific information through narration, visuals, interactive models, and simple storytelling.
  • Interactive learning: Encourages users to explore, observe, and test their knowledge rather than passively read information.
  • Reliable information: Uses authentic NASA photographs, coordinates, 3D models, and mission records.
  • Preservation of history: Brings attention to forgotten space missions and the technological achievements behind them.
  • Accessible AI assistance: Allows visitors to ask questions and receive answers grounded in NASA's official archives.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main goal is to preserve the stories of humanity's forgotten space explorers and make space history accessible to a wider audience, especially younger generations.

We want people to understand that space exploration does not end when communication with a spacecraft is lost or when a mission is completed. These machines represent years of human research, engineering, ambition, and discovery.

By giving these silent machines a voice through C.U.R.I.O., we transform archived scientific information into an emotional and educational experience. Ultimately, we hope to encourage curiosity about space, appreciation for scientific heritage, and interest in future exploration.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We developed the project as a web-based application using the following technologies:We also used AI-assisted video production to create Vox-style explanatory films using authentic NASA imagery and mission information.

  • Frontend: React 19, JavaScript
  • Build tool: Vite 6
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS v4
  • Animations: Framer Motion 12
  • 3D visualization: Google Model Viewer, NASA GLB models
  • AI assistant: OpenAI API (GPT-4o-mini)
  • Information retrieval: Custom BM25 algorithm (RAG system)
  • Voice generation: ElevenLabs API (Vincent voice)
  • Audio effects: Web Audio API
  • NASA data: NASA Image and Video Library API, NSSDCA, JPL Photojournal, NASA 3D Resources
  • Video production: AI-assisted generation, motion graphics, NASA archival imagery
  • Hosting: Vercel
  • Version control: Git / GitHub
  • Hardware: No dedicated hardware required; web-based application.

  • 5. How is your project creative?

Our creativity lies in transforming NASA's scientific archives into an immersive space adventure rather than a traditional educational experience.

  • Immersive design: A complete retro-futuristic visual identity with planetary environments, film grain, scanlines, animated interfaces, and cinematic warp transitions.
  • Sound experience: Original sound effects generated in real time, making every interaction—from radar signals to space travel and stamp collection—feel alive.
  • Interactive 3D: Real NASA mission models that visitors can rotate, inspect, and explore.
  • AI-generated films: Vox-style documentaries combining real NASA imagery, motion graphics, and narration, designed to capture Gen Z's attention and make space science exciting.
  • Gamification: Visitors embark on an exploration journey, discover forgotten machines, complete quizzes, and collect passport stamps to earn the title of Universal Astronaut.
  • C.U.R.I.O. AI personality: A warm, funny, old-fashioned robotic caretaker who guides visitors and answers their questions.
  • Reliable AI assistant: Our RAG-based system retrieves information from a curated NASA knowledge base, ensuring answers are source-grounded, cited, and transparent when information is unavailable.

Our vision is to make learning feel like an adventure: combining science, storytelling, design, sound, and technology to inspire a new generation to discover the wonders of NASA.
